## State Summary

**Scope:** Read-only harvest of current OSPF/IS-IS state on `ceos1` (1.1.1.1) and `ceos2` (2.2.2.2), scoped to the point-to-point link (Ethernet1, area 0.0.0.0) and Loopback0 per this leg's design needs. **Completeness: FULL** — all planned reads succeeded, no partial/failed calls. **IS-IS existence check: CONFIRMED ABSENT on both devices** (expected outcome per contract `existenceAssumptions.p1Harvest`).

**Self-provisioning:** Descriptor fetched via Browser Automation Service from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paichart/paichart/main/descriptors/ceos-lab-readonly-descriptor.json`. Registered service `ceos-lab-readonly` (id `cmtatloee000cyxe02wf7xd9d`) → endpoint `https://ceos-lab.paichart.app/mcp`, category `automation`, tools `list_devices`/`fetch_data`/`show_commands` (show_commands allowlist-constrained). Landed `ACTIVE` immediately (auto-approving category) — no update step needed. Health check: ACTIVE, 100% success rate. **Teardown deferred to SYNTHESIZE** per protocol — service intentionally NOT deleted this run.

**Secret hygiene:** the `config` (running) NAPALM getter returned two secret-bearing lines per device — a local `username admin ... secret sha512 $6$...` hash and an `snmp-server community ... ro` cleartext string. Neither is reproduced below; both are redacted to placeholders. No plaintext secret value is restated anywhere in this report.

---

### 1. OSPF neighbor state (point-to-point link, Ethernet1)

**Command:** `show ip ospf neighbor` — **Device: ceos1**
```
Neighbor ID     Instance VRF      Pri State                  Dead Time   Address         Interface
2.2.2.2         1        default  0   FULL                   00:00:34    10.0.12.2       Ethernet1
```

**Command:** `show ip ospf neighbor` — **Device: ceos2**
```
Neighbor ID     Instance VRF      Pri State                  Dead Time   Address         Interface
1.1.1.1         1        default  0   FULL                   00:00:37    10.0.12.1       Ethernet1
```

Adjacency is FULL bidirectionally over Ethernet1 — healthy OSPF baseline.

### 2. OSPF interface state + cost (area 0 baseline)

**Command:** `show ip ospf interface brief` — **Device: ceos1**
```
   Interface          Instance VRF        Area            IP Address         Cost  State      Nbrs
   Lo0                1        default    0.0.0.0         1.1.1.1/32         10    DR         0
   Et1                1        default    0.0.0.0         10.0.12.1/30       10    P2P        1
```

**Command:** `show ip ospf interface brief` — **Device: ceos2**
```
   Interface          Instance VRF        Area            IP Address         Cost  State      Nbrs
   Lo0                1        default    0.0.0.0         2.2.2.2/32         10    DR         0
   Et1                1        default    0.0.0.0         10.0.12.2/30       10    P2P        1
```

Both Ethernet1 and Loopback0 are in area 0.0.0.0; Ethernet1 network type is P2P (point-to-point, matches contract); **interface cost = 10 on both sides** — matches `interfaceMetrics.values` in the Program Interface Contract exactly (no discrepancy to report).

### 3. IS-IS process existence check

**Command:** `show isis neighbor` — **Device: ceos1**
```
(empty output)
```
**Command:** `show isis neighbor` — **Device: ceos2**
```
(empty output)
```
Corroborated by the absence of any `router isis` stanza in either device's running-config (§4 below). **No IS-IS process exists on either device** — CREATE is the correct downstream action, consistent with contract expectation.

### 4. Interface config — Ethernet1 and Loopback0 (+ OSPF process), verbatim from `fetch_data(getters:["config"], getters_options:{config:{retrieve:"running"}})`

**Device: ceos1** (secrets redacted; interface/OSPF stanzas quoted exactly as returned)
```
username admin privilege 15 role network-admin secret sha512 <<REDACTED-SECRET>>
!
snmp-server community <<REDACTED-SECRET>> ro
!
interface Ethernet1
   description to-ceos2 (ospf cost 10)
   no switchport
   ip address 10.0.12.1/30
   ip ospf cost 10
   ip ospf network point-to-point
!
interface Loopback0
   description router-id / migration anchor
   ip address 1.1.1.1/32
!
router ospf 1
   router-id 1.1.1.1
   passive-interface Loopback0
   network 1.1.1.1/32 area 0.0.0.0
   network 10.0.12.0/30 area 0.0.0.0
   max-lsa 12000
```

**Device: ceos2** (secrets redacted; interface/OSPF stanzas quoted exactly as returned)
```
username admin privilege 15 role network-admin secret sha512 <<REDACTED-SECRET>>
!
snmp-server community <<REDACTED-SECRET>> ro
!
interface Ethernet1
   description to-ceos1 (ospf cost 10)
   no switchport
   ip address 10.0.12.2/30
   ip ospf cost 10
   ip ospf network point-to-point
!
interface Loopback0
   description router-id / migration anchor
   ip address 2.2.2.2/32
!
router ospf 1
   router-id 2.2.2.2
   passive-interface Loopback0
   network 2.2.2.2/32 area 0.0.0.0
   network 10.0.12.0/30 area 0.0.0.0
   max-lsa 12000
```

**Notable finding vs. contract:** the OSPF baseline in the contract states `interfaceCost: 10` at the link level but the harvested config sets cost via `ip ospf cost 10` directly under Ethernet1 (not via a process-wide default) — consistent, no conflict. Loopback0 is `passive-interface` under OSPF, matching `loopbackPassive.rule` (carried over to IS-IS is a P1 design task, not observed here). Router-IDs (1.1.1.1 / 2.2.2.2), Loopback0 addressing, link subnet (10.0.12.0/30) and per-side addressing (.1 / .2) all match the Program Interface Contract exactly — reported as an observation, not assumed.

---

## Cross-check against Program Interface Contract (observation only, not reconciliation)

| Contract value | Harvested value | Match |
|---|---|---|
| link subnet 10.0.12.0/30 | 10.0.12.1/30 (ceos1 Et1), 10.0.12.2/30 (ceos2 Et1) | ✅ |
| ceos1 routerId 1.1.1.1, Loopback0 1.1.1.1/32 | router-id 1.1.1.1, Lo0 1.1.1.1/32 | ✅ |
| ceos2 routerId 2.2.2.2, Loopback0 2.2.2.2/32 | router-id 2.2.2.2, Lo0 2.2.2.2/32 | ✅ |
| ospfBaseline.area 0.0.0.0 | area 0.0.0.0 on both interfaces | ✅ |
| ospfBaseline.interfaceCost 10 | cost 10 on both Et1 (interface brief + running-config) | ✅ |
| ospfBaseline.networkType point-to-point | Et1 state P2P, `ip ospf network point-to-point` configured | ✅ |
| existenceAssumptions.p1Harvest: no IS-IS process | confirmed absent both devices | ✅ |
| bgp: NONE | no `router bgp` stanza observed in either running-config | ✅ (no ASN entries below) |

No contradictions found between observed device state and the binding contract constants for this leg.

```json
## Harvested Allocations
[
  {"kind": "cidr", "cidr": "10.0.12.0/30", "device": "ceos1", "interface": "Ethernet1", "source": "fetch_data(config, retrieve=running) — network 10.0.12.0/30 area 0.0.0.0 (router ospf 1)"},
  {"kind": "cidr", "cidr": "10.0.12.1/30", "device": "ceos1", "interface": "Ethernet1", "source": "fetch_data(config, retrieve=running) — interface Ethernet1: ip address 10.0.12.1/30"},
  {"kind": "cidr", "cidr": "10.0.12.0/30", "device": "ceos2", "interface": "Ethernet1", "source": "fetch_data(config, retrieve=running) — network 10.0.12.0/30 area 0.0.0.0 (router ospf 1)"},
  {"kind": "cidr", "cidr": "10.0.12.2/30", "device": "ceos2", "interface": "Ethernet1", "source": "fetch_data(config, retrieve=running) — interface Ethernet1: ip address 10.0.12.2/30"},
  {"kind": "cidr", "cidr": "1.1.1.1/32", "device": "ceos1", "interface": "Loopback0", "source": "fetch_data(config, retrieve=running) — interface Loopback0: ip address 1.1.1.1/32; also network 1.1.1.1/32 area 0.0.0.0"},
  {"kind": "cidr", "cidr": "2.2.2.2/32", "device": "ceos2", "interface": "Loopback0", "source": "fetch_data(config, retrieve=running) — interface Loopback0: ip address 2.2.2.2/32; also network 2.2.2.2/32 area 0.0.0.0"}
]
```

No `asn`-kind entries: neither device runs BGP (no `router bgp` stanza observed, consistent with contract `"bgp": "NONE"`); OSPF process ID 1 is a process identifier, not an AS number, and is not recorded as an allocation.

**Handoff note:** Service `ceos-lab-readonly` remains registered/ACTIVE for downstream re-use if needed within this leg; teardown (`registry.delete`) executes at SYNTHESIZE per protocol, regardless of approve/escalate outcome.

Confidence: 95 — All eight scoped read-only calls succeeded with literal, verbatim output; IS-IS absence corroborated two ways (empty neighbor output + no `router isis` stanza in config); every contract-bound value cross-checked with zero discrepancies. Minor uncertainty only in not having independently probed `show isis database`/`show isis hostname` (redundant given config-level confirmation of no IS-IS process), which is why this isn't 100.
